{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./NN_03-01.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from LSF:
#   -q gpuv100                      -> (not translated; site-specific queue)
#   -gpu "num=1:mode=exclusive_process" -> -g 1  (exclusive mode not translated)
#   -n 5                            -> -n 1 -c 5  (single task, 5 CPU cores)
#   -R "span[hosts=1]"             -> -N 1
#   -W 20:00                        -> -t 20h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 5 -g 1 -t 20h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: LSF -q gpuv100 not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible GPU resources; you are not forcing the gpuv100 queue.

  # NOTE: LSF GPU mode exclusive_process not translated.
  # Performance implication: without exclusive GPU allocation semantics, GPU sharing could occur (if the site allows it), potentially reducing performance.

  # NOTE: LSF -R "rusage[mem=6GB]" (memory per core) not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: LSF -J NN_03-01 not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance unaffected.

  # NOTE: LSF -o output/NN_03-01-%J.out not translated.
  # Flux does not portably provide LSF %J expansion in output paths.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: logs may overwrite unless you generate unique filenames.

  # NOTE: LSF -B/-N (email at start/stop) not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

  module purge
  module load tensorflow/1.5-gpu-python-3.6.2

  # Run within the allocation.
  flux run -n 1 -c 5 -g 1 bash -lc '
    for drop in 0.2 0.25 0.3 0.4; do
      for N in 250 350 400 450 550; do
        for nhidden in 6; do
          for act in sigmoid; do
            for folder in "03-01-2019 11.04" "09-01-2019 12.57" "11-10-2018 11.36"; do
              for func in group_period_x_group_period group_period_2x2 atomic_number; do
                python3 NN/NN_script.py "$drop" "$N" sigmoid 6 "$folder" "$func"
              done
            done
          done
        done
      done
    done
  '
fi
"
}
